title: Linus Torvalds posts his first AI-assisted patch to the Linux kernel, synthetic test clocks 23x performance leap — the bossman makes use of AI tooling himself after issuing clear pro-AI directives
key_facts: Linus Torvalds has posted what Tom's Hardware calls his own first LLM-assisted patch, in a development branch.
It targets cache contention when many CPUs read the same file, which can arise with shared libraries, databases and web servers.
Several developers tried to fix the issue over the years with varied results; Torvalds posted his own draft in early 2024 and has used it on his laptop since.
He recently decided to 'try to actually solve this thing using an LLM'.
He claims a 23x performance improvement in a dedicated synthetic benchmark but notes real-world impact will be far smaller, since 'no real load' will see those figures.
Tom's Hardware guesses server workloads would benefit more than desktops.
The kernel team is changing its policy to no longer require patch authors to disclose AI tool use; Torvalds likens LLMs to compilers or editors.
AI agents spotting common security flaw patterns made the Linux security mailing list 'unmanageable' earlier in the year.
quote_evidence: After a few revisions of his position on AI-assisted contributions to the Linux kernel, Linus Torvalds has posted his own first LLM-assisted patch.

He's now posted his solution in a development branch, and claims that he's seen a 23x performance improvement in a dedicated synthetic benchmark, though he notes that actual real-world impact will be far less significant, as "no real load" will witness those figures.
why_it_matters_hint: The head of the Linux kernel is now using an AI coding tool himself on a long-standing performance problem, though the gain is only shown in a test and the patch is not merged.
event_date: Commit dated about 10 Oct 2026 per Linuxiac; widely reported 12 to 13 Oct
notes: Older news re-dated: Tom's Hardware ran it 16 Oct; ZDNET and Linuxiac covered it 12 to 13 Oct. 23x versus about 3x discrepancy noted.
